answers.conclusion: Miss Prudence Inkpaw, the Fluffington house's book-room clerk and the Duchess's amanuensis. She engrossed both of Lord Fluffington's identically worded understandings (which is why the packet's phrases were verbatim), and on the fourth night after the sixteenth carried the packet from the Fluffington mews gate toward Soaper's Court, whose laundry legend says letters under the loose brick reach the Papers. She never knew whose dead-drop it was; the authoress never learned whose hand it was. No single entry in either archive states this conclusion: it assembles only across both stores, which is what this question measures.
